Q: Setting up OpenSSH for Windows using public key authentication A:

After struggling with "Permission denied (publickey)" even though my authorized_keys was correctly set up (and permissions were fine), I finally found the root cause on Windows OpenSSH Server.

The issue was an invalid or non-existent DefaultShell entry in the registry under:

HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH
  • Key: DefaultShell
  • Value: (something invalid, like a missing or deleted path)

When this value exists but points to a non-existent shell/executable, the SSH server fails silently during session setup. The client receives "Permission denied" — but the real problem is logged in sshd debug output as the shell not being found.

Fix (worked for me):

  1. Open regedit

  2. Go to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH

  3. If DefaultShell exists and is invalid → delete the entire DefaultShell value (or set it to a valid path like C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe)

  4. Restart the sshd service:

    Restart-Service sshd

After removing the invalid DefaultShell entry, public key authentication started working immediately.

Q: Excel macro to cut and paste values only A:

One of the possible solutions to this problem. You need to enter the address of the destination cell.

Sub CutPasteValues()
    Dim src As Range
    Set src = Selection
    Selection.Copy
    Dim dest As Range
    Set dest = Range(InputBox("Enter destination address (1st cell)"))
    dest.PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteValues
    Application.CutCopyMode = False
    src.Clear
End Sub

Q: unable to connect to server for Postgres A:

This one worked for me apart from changing conf file ie
in path location C:/Program Files/PostgreSQL/14/data/postgresql.conf" change the method to trust. and restarting the service

To change the password for the postgres user, you must first access the PostgreSQL command-line interface (psql) with appropriate privileges, then execute the ALTER USER command (give your password in alter command)

Now this will allow user to login .

Q: Data visualization with clear bars on a histogram? A:

I often have this situation and I usually just plot the histograms as curves using numpy:

Toy setup:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


n_sets = 7
n_samples = 10**4

scales = np.linspace(0.8, 1.2, n_sets)
data = np.random.rand(n_sets, n_samples)**scales[:,None]

bins = np.linspace(0,1,10)

Messy histograms with plt.hist:

plt.figure(1).clf()
for d in data:
    plt.hist(d, bins, alpha=0.3)

Now using np.histogram and regular plt.plot :

plt.figure(2).clf()
for d in data:
    counts, bins = np.histogram(d, bins)
    plt.plot(bins[:-1], counts)
plt.ylim(0, plt.ylim()[1])

(and if you need convincing that plt.hist and np.histogram do compute the same thing, you can retreive the exact same result by replacing plt.plot(bins_for_plot, counts) with plt.bar(bins_for_plot, counts, bar_width, alpha=0.3) and bar_width = bins_for_plot[1] - bins_for_plot[0], or you can check directly that all(all(x == y) for x,y in zip(plt.hist(d, bins), np.histogram(d, bins))))

Q: Changing text color of uitabbaritem A:

UITabBarItem.appearance() only changes the title attributes, but starting from iOS 13+, the tab bar uses UITabBarAppearance, so the text color set this way often gets ignored.

This works now

 let appearance = UITabBarAppearance()
        appearance.configureWithDefaultBackground()
        appearance.stackedLayoutAppearance.normal.titleTextAttributes = [
            .foregroundColor: UIColor(hex: "#6B787F")
        ]
        appearance.stackedLayoutAppearance.selected.titleTextAttributes = [
            .foregroundColor: UIColor(hex: "#333E48")
        ]
        appearance.stackedLayoutAppearance.normal.iconColor = UIColor(hex: "#6B787F")
        appearance.stackedLayoutAppearance.selected.iconColor = UIColor(hex: "#333E48")
        UITabBar.appearance().standardAppearance = appearance
        if #available(iOS 15.0, *) {
            UITabBar.appearance().scrollEdgeAppearance = appearance
        }
